reading.body:
A mistagged OpenStreetMap point for a former software office is being counted as an Arizona data center, and it should not be.

The record carries zero megawatts and no operator. Emailage was a fraud-prevention and email-risk-scoring software company, acquired by LexisNexis Risk Solutions, that ran on cloud and outsourced infrastructure rather than its own colocation or hosting. A reverse geocode of the stored coordinates now returns a different tenant, Safe T Professionals LLC, at 25 South Arizona Place in Chandler. The point was tagged as a data center and the building underneath it has since turned over.

This matters because facility counts are the denominator for everything downstream. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, only 4 of which publish capacity figures, totaling 512 MW. A phantom entry inflates the count without adding a single megawatt, which makes the state's compute footprint look broader than the published capacity can support. The gap between 56 facilities and 4 with numbers is the real story, and this row widens it.

What the data does not say is how many other entries share this problem. One mistagged point is documented here, and the research status is exhausted, meaning no source ties this address to server or hosting infrastructure. That is a statement about this address only. It is not evidence about the other 55 Arizona facilities, and it does not tell the reader whether the 512 MW figure is complete or representative.
